key_insight: This review explains how laser-arc hybrid welding combines the deep penetration of lasers with the gap-bridging ability of arc welding to improve joining quality in high-performance steels.
engineering_relevance: It is relevant for designing faster, more robust welding processes for advanced steels used in structural, transportation, and energy applications.
method: Reviews process mechanisms in laser-arc interaction and joint formation
Summarizes performance-enhancement strategies across parameters and material responses
Synthesizes reported improvements in weld quality, efficiency, and defect control
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates a review article indexed in OpenAlex and published in the Journal of Manufacturing Processes, but does not provide experimental dataset details or quantitative evaluation in the abstract.
watch_item: Because this is a review, implementation guidance depends on the specific steel grade, thickness, and laser-arc setup, so process transferability may be limited without case-specific validation.
paper_title: A comprehensive review on laser-arc hybrid welding of high-performance steels: From process mechanisms to performance enhancement
